Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

sermon noun

also homily, preaching, give a sermon

late Latin

Aug. Sermōnēs ad populum
M-O s.v. preach: sermon

sermō, sermōnis m.

noun, third declension

a sermon

Classically talk or conversation; Augustine’s word for his sermons to the people. To preach a sermon is sermōnem ad populum habēre (Egger, in Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • homīlia, homīliae f. — a homily

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Traupman 376

    Greek ὁμιλία, a talk; the usual word for a sermon that explains the day’s Gospel.

Examples

  • homīliam habēre

    to give a sermonTraupman 376

See also priest, church, Mass, the Divine Liturgy.

SourcesLewis & Short: sermo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 376, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. preach: sermon.

Homīlia is not in Lewis & Short; its quantities are Traupman’s.
